solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prepares space for game of golf in grounds

indicators.note: one thing put 'for' another stands in its place, so the space takes over from the game here

parts.note: taken as the word itself
a round is one game of golf
room means space

explanation.surface: A groundsman readies an area of the grounds for a round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' here means 'in place of': the space replaces the game within the grounds, not a space set aside for playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom something is to tidy and ready it, a synonym of prepares.

clue.text: Male boxer possibly making a comeback with different sponsor

indicators.note: coming back means the dog is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog, hence 'possibly'
other means different

explanation.surface: A male fighter returns to the ring with a new backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' is not a fighter but a breed of dog, which is what makes the comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A godmother is a sponsor at a baptism, vouching for the child's religious upbringing.

clue.text: Compound in hydrogen-depleted animal skin

indicators.note: depleted means lacking, so the hydrogen symbol is removed from the skin

parts.note: oxhide is the hide of an ox
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A chemist finds some compound in a hide that has lost its hydrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the H out of OXHIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen with another element.

clue.text: Consider change for the better, inspired by spouse

indicators.note: inspired literally means breathed in, so the edit goes inside the spouse

parts.note: a mate is a husband or wife
to edit is to revise and improve

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about self-improvement prompted by their partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to think deeply, a synonym of consider.

clue.text: Pig crate needs repair — details of damage on label

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A pig's crate is broken and a label records the damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damage' is British slang for cost, as in 'what's the damage?'
explanation.definitionFit: A price tag is a label stating the cost, which is the slang 'damage'.

clue.text: He wrote the story our disheartened bloke adapted

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters are rearranged
losing its heart leaves only the outside letters of bloke

parts.note: first and last letters give BE

explanation.surface: A man rewrites a story for publication.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOKE without its middle LOK leaves BE; THE STORY, OUR and BE rearranged give the poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Southey, English Poet Laureate, was the author of The Story of the Three Bears.

clue.text: Part of shirt buttonhole

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the band round the neck of a shirt
second meaning: to buttonhole someone is to accost and detain them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Buttonhole' looks like another part of the shirt, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the neckband of a shirt and, as a verb, means to accost or waylay someone.

clue.text: Recorded number on case for trainer's loose kit

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a track is a recorded song on an album
a suit is a case at law

explanation.surface: A recorded song is played over a case for a trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trainer' is an athlete or coach, whose kit is loose sportswear.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracksuit is the loose two-piece outfit worn by athletes for training.

clue.text: Gun with enamelled casing kept within college

parts.note: gat is old slang for a gun

indicators.note: the casing of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters give ED

explanation.surface: A gun in an enamelled case is locked away at college.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge, a student who is gated is confined to college as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being gated is a punishment in which a student is confined to the college grounds.

clue.text: Exhausted, failed to play one's part?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: run out, used up
second meaning: an actor who dries up forgets lines

explanation.walkthrough: An actor who dries up forgets lines on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried up means used up, and in theatre slang it means an actor forgot their lines.

clue.text: Want no unpaid help to initiate action?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: to like being charged for help rather than getting it free
second meaning: to bring a formal legal accusation

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, to prefer charges is to want to be billed, so unpaid help is not wanted; in law it means to bring an accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: Preferring charges is the legal step of formally accusing someone, which starts proceedings.

clue.text: A line slipped into big report for added weight

indicators.note: slipped into means put inside, so A and the line go within the report

parts.note: a blast is a loud bang

explanation.surface: A sentence is inserted into a weighty report to bulk it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' is a bang, not a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballast is heavy material carried to give a ship stability, extra weight.

clue.text: Finished last in event, that's clear

parts.note: over means finished

indicators.note: the last letter in the word event is taken

parts.note: last letter gives T

explanation.surface: Someone came last in a competition, plain for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, the same as clear.

clue.text: Set aside organ, one of two not in pristine condition

parts.note: an ear is an organ, and we each have two
something marked is blemished

explanation.surface: An organ, one of a pair, is put aside because it is damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Earmarked means designated or reserved for a purpose, as funds are set aside.

clue.text: Catch kid adopting Linnaeus's term for pansy

parts.note: to catch a sound is to hear it

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the kid takes in the letter

parts.note: to kid is to tease

indicators.note: a term is an end, so the last letter of Linnaeus's is taken

parts.note: last letter gives S

explanation.surface: Someone teasing a child picks up the botanist Linnaeus's word for the pansy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linnaeus's term' looks like a botanical name, but 'term' means end: its final S goes into TEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartsease is the old common name of the wild pansy, Viola tricolor.

clue.text: Like the solvers, the setters are back to square one

parts.note: the solvers are addressed as 'you', so like them is as you
setters speak of themselves as 'we', and we are is we're

explanation.surface: Solvers and setters alike find themselves back where they started.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of WE'RE is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: 'As you were' is the military order to return to the previous position, an idiom for starting again.

clue.text: Workers' groups put together gear for Kirov, perhaps

indicators.note: put together means joined side by side, so the two unions are placed next to each other

parts.note: TU, a trade union, a workers' group
the plural asks for a second TU

explanation.surface: Unions combine to equip the Kirov.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kirov is the famous St Petersburg ballet company, not a political body.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short stiff skirt worn by ballerinas, such as dancers of the Kirov Ballet.

clue.text: One who's up robing duke with unusual grandeur

indicators.note: robing means clothing, so the rearranged letters wrap round the duke
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A duke is dressed in strange splendour.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'up' is to be in residence at university.
explanation.definitionFit: An undergraduate student is said to be 'up' at university during term.

clue.text: Minds out for shocking gymnast's last move?

indicators.note: shocking means appalling, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An onlooker warns people to mind themselves at a startling gymnastic finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismount is the final move by which a gymnast leaves the apparatus.

clue.text: One's told to heighten beams

indicators.note: what one is told is heard spoken, so the word for heighten is taken by its sound

parts.note: to raise is to heighten

explanation.surface: Someone is instructed to raise some beams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beams' looks like timbers to lift; it is beams of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are beams of light or radiation.

clue.text: Familiar master, inwardly curious, heading for dormitory

indicators.note: inwardly means within, so curious goes inside master

parts.note: an ace is an expert, a master
quaint means curious, odd

indicators.note: the head of the word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter gives D

explanation.surface: A familiar schoolmaster, oddly curious, goes off to the dormitory.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquainted with something means knowing it, being familiar with it.

clue.text: Reduce drill (cut by hour)

indicators.note: being cut by something means it slices into the middle

parts.note: to sink a well or shaft is to drill it

explanation.surface: A drill bit is cut down to size in an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink is to become or make smaller, a synonym of reduce.

clue.text: Solution for hygienist opening laundry

parts.note: a mouth is an opening
a wash is a load of laundry

explanation.surface: A dental hygienist solves the problem of opening a laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' is a liquid, not an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouthwash is a liquid rinse that a dental hygienist might recommend.

clue.text: Single decoration, apt reward when viewed in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back means reading the letters in reverse

parts.note: fit means apt, suitable
OM is the Order of Merit, an honour

explanation.surface: A single medal looks like a fitting reward in hindsight.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a single decorative design or pattern element.

clue.text: Gardening aid welcomed by more women on retirement

indicators.note: on retirement says the hidden letters are read backwards
welcomed by means held inside, so the letters lie within more women

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Women who retire are given gardening equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'welcomed' into the definition, but 'welcomed by' is what says the letters sit inside 'more women'; the definition is just 'Gardening aid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mower is a machine for cutting lawns, a tool for gardening.

clue.text: Go to and fro aboard carrier

parts.note: to wag is to move to and fro, as a tail does
on means aboard

explanation.surface: Something swings back and forth on board a carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a vehicle for transporting goods, a carrier.

clue.text: Bountiful dynasty needing initial support, of course

indicators.note: the dynasty needs the support placed before it

parts.note: a tee supports the ball for the first shot on a golf course
Ming was a Chinese dynasty

explanation.surface: A wealthy dynasty needs early help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' means on a golf course, where each hole starts from a tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeming means full to overflowing, abundant like something bountiful.

clue.text: Junior guy, one mixed up with Resistance

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A young man gets involved with the Resistance movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Younger means junior in age, the less senior of two.

clue.text: Malformed sardines maybe, about a kilo netted

indicators.note: fish netted are caught inside, so the fish encloses these letters

parts.note: sardines are an example of fish
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Some misshapen sardines, about a kilo, are caught in a net.
explanation.definitionFit: Freakish means abnormal or deformed, like something malformed.

clue.text: Paid our dues when we dined with daughter?

parts.note: at one o'clock, the traditional time for lunch

explanation.surface: A family settles the bill after dining with their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At one' is one o'clock, lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoned means made amends for wrongdoing, settling a moral debt.
